title: Annotatio II §.IV open: CONCEPTIO error 2 — middle-ages Fathers vs Eutyches absorption
pass_a_gloss: §. IV. To the first error succeeded a SECOND — namely a perverse understanding and interpretation of the Fathers of the Middle Ages after Chalcedon, that is the last Ecumenical Council opposed to Eutyches, who in fighting his heresy used among other arguments also this: that Christ’s human nature, even exalted, after personal Union with the divine, is not absorbed by the Divine more than bread is absorbed by Christ’s body in the legitimate use of the Eucharist, when united to it.
pass_b_english: §.IV: after the first error comes a SECOND — middle-ages Fathers after Chalcedon, read askew.
Fighting Eutyches they said Christ’s exalted human nature is not absorbed by the divine more than bread is absorbed by Christ’s body in legitimate Eucharistic use.
source_text: §. IV. Errori primo successit SECUNDUS, perversa scil. intelligentia ac interpretatio Patrum Mediorum Seculorum, post Chalcedonense scil. seu postremum Concilium Oecumenicum, Eutychi oppositum, istius hæresin verò impugnantium argumento inter alia eô quoque, quô humanam Christi naturam ne exaltatam quidem, post Unionem cum divina personalem, à Divina magis absorberi statuerunt, quàm panis absorbetur à corpore Christi, in legitimo Eucharistiæ usu, isti uniendo.
